scope.scores: Generated using the existing comprehensive-quiz scoring function; no bank, scoring, validator or UI code changes.
scope.publication: Integrated into the local generated catalogue. No remote deployment, commit or PR performed.
scope.images: Optional ideology images omitted; no image credits added.

method.procedure: docs/personality assessments/NEW_PROFILE.md; 12Axes-style sourced question-by-question assessment adapted to this project’s own questions and scoring.
method.specificVariants: Every subject has an explicit doctrine, regional or historical scope and period. This is not a survey of all adherents.
method.separateReviews: Each 240-answer assessment received a separate agent evidence review. Reviews corrected literal wording, direction, inference, source dates and government implementation claims before archiving.
method.contemporaryEvidence: Recent government acts and reporting corroborate relevant contemporary variants; foundational doctrines are not redefined as the positions of an incumbent government. Manifestos, announcements, allocations, implemented acts and reported allegations are distinguished in the source records.
method.neutralInterpretation: The user authorised complete representative assessments and neutral answers. Neutral responses explicitly model mixed or conditional judgements, principled non-ranking, or rejection of both premises where explained. They are not measurements of empirical causal equality. Historical modern-technology responses are disclosed analogies.
method.questionnaireFit: Stateless communism and social anarchism do not fit every question’s state, taxation and wage premises. Their explained neutral midpoints must not be read as ideological moderation. Some narrow human-trait comparisons are non-ranking representative models, not documented scientific positions.
method.similarity: All pairwise scores examined; only civic-nationalism and liberal-feminism exceed 95%. Both revision-one records contain reciprocal scope-retention decisions. No answers tuned to reduce similarity.
method.limitations: Separate review and structural validation do not certify the accuracy of every interpretation. The underlying question bank remains in development.

similarityDecisions.reason: Reviewed revision 1 of both profiles after independent literal-question and evidence checks. Retain both scoped subjects despite the diagnostic overlap: Scottish SNP civic nationalism centres national self-determination and residence-based membership, whereas US egalitarian liberal feminism centres gendered autonomy, equal political agency and reform of care institutions. The current questions capture much shared liberal and social-democratic policy, so similar coordinates do not establish doctrinal identity. Ownership, military, fiscal and secession responses retain evidence-based distinctions; source-supported values were not tuned to create distance. This decision is a named scope-retention judgement, not a claim that all civic nationalists or feminists share either profile.
